rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ally ambiguity 1: is a creature its own ally?
rulings_proposed.ruling: Reading A: a creature is never its own ally. Effects that include the user say 'you or an ally'. So a rogue next to the target doesn't count as an ally for her own Sneak Attack, and Help can't assist the helper's own check.

rulings_proposed.ambiguity: GLOSS.ally gap: 'your friend' has no game state
rulings_proposed.ruling: A creature whose attitude toward the party is Friendly (the GLOSS.influence attitudes) is the party's friend and so its ally, even if it isn't fighting on a side. An Indifferent or Hostile creature isn't a friend.

summary: I added 16 GLOSS.ally tests to tests/srd/test_glossary.py. Each clause is tested through its effects: Sneak Attack's ally within 5 ft, Help on an attack roll, Pack Tactics, controlled mounts, and the Session attack and spawn commands. 12 pass and 4 are strict xfail (red): (1) Help's ability-check assist accepts the helper as their own ally; (2) Help's ability-check assist accepts an enemy; (3) a Friendly-attitude NPC is never an ally, because allies are team-only; (4) a monster spawned through the Session with team='party' crashes the next command (Monster has no 'wielded'). I proposed two rulings: you aren't your own ally, and a Friendly attitude means 'friend'. One infra ticket: there's no GM command to re-designate a creature's side mid-encounter. I added two cheats to the abuse catalogue. One mistake on the way: a sed of mine briefly rewrote 11 assertions in the existing prone tests. I reverted it, and git diff now shows only additions. tests/srd passes with 389 passed and 4 xfailed, and ruff check and ruff format are clean.
